questions.context: Last year, the manager promised that the bank will approve my loan.
questions.instruction: Rewrite the full sentence with the error corrected.
questions.correctAnswer: Last year, the manager promised that the bank would approve my loan.
questions.explanation: The promise was made in the past, so reported 'will' shifts to 'would': 'promised that the bank would approve'.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: Last year, the manager promised that the bank can approve my loan.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: You changed the modal, but 'can' doesn't fit a past reported promise; 'would' is needed.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: Last year, the manager promised that the bank will have approved my loan.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: This adds a future perfect form; the reported promise simply needs 'would'.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: Last year, the manager promised that the bank would to approve my loan.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: You changed the modal but added 'to'; modals are followed by the bare verb.

questions.context: You should to check your bank balance before you shop online.
questions.instruction: Rewrite the full sentence with the error corrected.
questions.correctAnswer: You should check your bank balance before you shop online.
questions.explanation: After a modal like 'should', we use the bare infinitive without 'to': 'should check'.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: You should checking your bank balance before you shop online.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: After 'should' you don't add -ing; use the plain base verb.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: You should to checking your bank balance before you shop online.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: You kept 'to' and added -ing; a modal needs just the base verb.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: You should checked your bank balance before you shop online.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: After a modal the verb stays in its base form, not the past.

questions.context: Ali got a job at a large company. He says that ___ salary is much higher than his old one, so he can save more.
questions.instruction: Fill in the blank with one word.
questions.explanation: We use 'the' because it's the specific salary of his new job, already clear from context.

commonWrongAnswers.comment: 'A' treats the salary as new information, but we know it's the salary of his new job.
'An' is used before vowel sounds, and this salary is a specific one, so it needs 'the'.

questions.context: I pay my rent yesterday, so I have no money left.
questions.instruction: Rewrite the full sentence with the error corrected.
questions.correctAnswer: I paid my rent yesterday, so I have no money left.
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' points to a finished past time, so we use the past simple: 'paid'.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: I have paid my rent yesterday, so I have no money left.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: Present perfect doesn't go with a finished time like 'yesterday'; use the past simple.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: I have paid my rent, so I have no money left yesterday.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: This moves 'yesterday' to the wrong clause; the paying happened yesterday.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: I was paying my rent yesterday, so I have no money left.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: Past continuous suggests an action in progress; here the payment was a completed event.

questions.context: Sara wants to save money, so she has decided to avoid ___ expensive coffee every morning. (buy)
questions.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct form of the verb.
questions.explanation: After 'avoid', the next verb takes -ing, so it's 'avoid buying'.

commonWrongAnswers.comment: It's tempting because 'decided' takes 'to', but 'avoid' is followed by -ing.
The base verb doesn't work after 'avoid'; use the -ing form.
